about.home.welcome.title: What it is
about.home.welcome.body: DND Character Maker helps you build, play and print Dungeons & Dragons 5th edition characters with the SRD 5.1 rules. It is free, needs no account, works offline once opened, and keeps your characters on this device.
about.home.flow.title: How it works
about.home.flow.body: Create guides you step by step: origin, class, ability scores, choices, spells, equipment and story. Sheet shows the finished character, Play is for the table (hit points, rests, spell slots, rolls) and Print makes paper or PDF. Free edit lets you override any number, and Level up is in Create and in Play.
about.home.share.title: Sharing and backup
about.home.share.body: Share makes a link, a QR code or a file that opens the character on another device. Export saves a character as a file and Import brings it back. Characters live only in this browser, so export them to keep a copy.
about.home.packs.title: Content packs
about.home.packs.body: Write your own homebrew with the editor (spells, items, feats, species, backgrounds, classes, subclasses), or add content from other tools: Aurora XML files, an index file or an address. What you add stays on your device. A pack made from files you imported can be removed but not exported or shared.
about.home.translation.title: Languages and translation
about.home.translation.body: The app speaks English, Italian, French, German and Spanish. The rules texts come from the official SRD translations; the few that are missing show in English. With your own DeepL key, Automatic translation translates them as you read and marks them. Distances follow the language, and can be changed at the top.
about.home.beta.title: This version
about.home.beta.body: Version {version}. It works, but it still needs a lot of testing: if something looks wrong, a number does not add up or a text is missing, tell us.
about.roadmap.intro: What is still missing, from the nearest to the furthest.
about.changelog.intro: What changed in each version, newest first.
translate.title: Automatic translation
translate.intro: Texts that have no translation in your language yet can be translated by DeepL as you read them. A translated text says so, and can be switched back to the English original. Translations are kept on this device, so each text is translated only once.
translate.english: Nothing to translate while the app is in English. Choose another language first.
translate.enable: Translate the texts that are still in English
translate.descOnlyHint: Machine translation does well with sentences and badly with a name on its own: without context, a name often comes out wrong. With this on, names stay in English and everything else is translated. It also uses fewer of your characters.
translate.keyHint: A free key (it ends in :fx) or a paid one, from your DeepL account. It stays on this device and travels to DeepL, through the relay, with each request.
translate.howTo: How to get a DeepL key
translate.howTo1: Make a free account for the DeepL API (not the ordinary translator app) at
translate.howTo2: Open your account and go to the API Keys tab: there is a key, ending in :fx if the plan is free.
translate.howTo3: Copy it and paste it in the box above. That is all.
translate.howToNote: The free plan has an allowance of characters, which DeepL may change; the page above says how much. A game's texts use little of it, and what is translated is kept on this device, so nothing is paid for twice.
translate.relayHint: DeepL does not accept requests straight from a web page, so they go through a small relay. The default one is run by the author of the app; it keeps neither your key nor your texts, and its code is in the repository. You can run your own: see
translate.clearConfirm: Delete {n} saved translations? They are translated again when needed.
translate.err.unreachable: The relay could not be reached. Check its address and your connection.
translate.err.refused: DeepL refused the key. Check that it is complete.
translate.err.limit: Too many requests at once. Wait a moment and open the text again.
translate.err.quota: The DeepL allowance is used up.
packs.title: Content packs
packs.intro: Besides the SRD 5.1 that comes with the app, you can add packs of your own: homebrew you write, or content from files you already have. They are kept only on this device.
packs.rights: Only add content you have the right to use. The app does not include or download any protected content, and a pack you added from your own files can be removed but never exported or shared.

Index files are followed and every file they list is fetched from the address in the index: you are responsible for what you add. Spells, items, languages, backgrounds, races, feats, classes and archetypes are read, processed in your browser and kept on this device. Rules the app cannot apply by itself keep their text.
credits.title: Credits and licenses
credits.rulesIntro: The rules text and data come from the System Reference Document, used under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license.
credits.dataText: The structured SRD data is derived from the 5e-database project (MIT License).
credits.translationsText: Translated rules texts come from the official translations of the SRD 5.1 published by Wizards of the Coast under the same Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license. They have been matched to the structured data by this project.
credits.designText: The layout of the character sheet and its set of pages (main sheet, story, feature cards, spell cards) are inspired by the class character sheets by Emmet Byrne. All artwork in this app is drawn from scratch; no artwork from those sheets is used.
credits.fontsText: Cinzel, EB Garamond and Inter, bundled under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 through Fontsource.
credits.softwareText: DND Character Maker is open source (MIT License). It is built with Preact, Vite and other open source projects.
credits.qr: QR codes are drawn with the MIT-licensed library by Kazuhiko Arase. QR Code is a registered trademark of DENSO WAVE INCORPORATED.
